docs.title: Ella IMS
docs.text: Ella IMS lets subscribers of a private 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. It is an IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) that runs as a single application, designed to be easy to operate, reliable, and secure.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Voice and video calls over 4G (VoLTE) and 5G (VoNR).
  • SIP trunks: connect your private network to the public phone network.
  • SIM-based authentication with your existing HSS (IMS-AKA over Cx), and IPsec between phones and the IMS.
  • Voice QoS from the 4G or 5G core: PCRF over Rx, or PCF over N5 with optional mutual TLS.
  • Application Servers: connect voicemail, conferencing, supplementary services and other services, routed per subscriber by your HSS (iFCs over ISC).
  • Push-to-talk: a built-in MCPTT server for group calls with floor control, and an Android client.
  • Call records: who called whom, when, for how long, and how the call ended.
  • Easy to operate: a single binary with an embedded database, a web UI, an HTTP API, and Prometheus metrics.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Ella IMS with Ella Core

An IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) is what lets phones on a 4G or 5G network make voice and video calls. The core network gives each phone an IP connection to the IMS. Over that connection, the phone registers and places calls with SIP, and the IMS routes them.

Ella IMS handles the signalling. The voice and video of a call go between the phones, through the core network. Calls over SIP trunks are the exception: their voice goes through Ella IMS.

docs.title: Three CSCFs in one process
docs.text:
3GPP splits the IMS's SIP routing into three Call Session Control Functions (CSCFs):

  • P-CSCF: the phone's first contact. It protects the phone's signalling with IPsec, and asks the core network for the QoS that voice and video need.
  • I-CSCF: the entry point of the network. It asks the HSS which S-CSCF serves a user.
  • S-CSCF: the registrar. It authenticates phones against the HSS, routes calls, and involves Application Servers when a subscriber's filter criteria say so.

In most IMS deployments, these are separate nodes. Ella IMS runs all three in one process, with one database, one UI and one API. Each CSCF still has its own SIP port, and the three exchange standard SIP messages, in memory, so from the outside Ella IMS looks like any other IMS.

docs.title: What Ella IMS relies on
docs.text:
Ella IMS relies on two functions of the core network:

  • The HSS holds the subscribers: their identities, the keys to authenticate them, and the filter criteria that bring in Application Servers. Ella IMS reaches it over Diameter (Cx).
  • The policy function has the core set up the dedicated bearers (4G) or QoS flows (5G) that carry voice and video. Ella IMS reaches it over Diameter (Rx), or a PCF over HTTP (N5).

Ella Core provides both. For how it works with an IMS, see Ella Core's IMS Integration.

docs.title: Who can call whom
docs.text:
Ella IMS connects calls between the subscribers its HSS knows. Calls to and from other numbers go over SIP trunks, to carriers such as PSTN providers or other operators. See SIP Trunks.

Ella IMS does not handle emergency calls.

docs.title: Push-to-Talk
docs.text: Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) is the 3GPP standard for group calls where one member talks at a time and the others listen. Ella IMS includes an MCPTT server, which runs in the same process as the CSCFs. Unlike a regular call, a group call's voice goes through Ella IMS, which copies each talker's audio to every listener.

docs.title: Users and groups
docs.text:
A "user" is a person, such as alice. A "group" gathers users who talk together, such as a team.

A user hears and talks in a group's calls once their app has joined the group.

docs.title: Authenticating phones
docs.text: Phones authenticate with the keys on their SIM, with IMS-AKA. When a phone registers, the S-CSCF fetches an authentication vector from the HSS, challenges the phone, and checks its answer. The phone checks the network in turn, so each side proves itself to the other.

docs.title: Protecting signalling with IPsec
docs.text:
The same authentication produces keys that the phone and the P-CSCF use to set up IPsec between them. From then on, the phone's SIP messages travel in ESP on dedicated ports. This protects the signalling from tampering, and ties every request to the phone that authenticated.

Ella IMS sets up these IPsec associations in the Linux kernel. That's why it needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, and why ESP must reach it through any firewall.

docs.title: The trust domain
docs.text:
SIP nodes tell each other who a request is from, for example with the P-Asserted-Identity header. A node believes this only from the nodes it trusts: its trust domain.

Phones are never trusted: the P-CSCF takes a phone's identity from its authentication.

Besides Ella IMS itself, the I-CSCF and the S-CSCF trust the networks in sip.trusted_networks, such as those of Application Servers. Trust goes by source address, so protect these networks, and keep the phones out of them.

docs.title: SIP trunks
docs.text:
Ella IMS accepts requests from a carrier only from its trunk's inbound CIDRs. Carriers are outside the trust domain, unless their trunk is trusted.

With TLS, Ella IMS checks the carrier's certificate on connections it opens to the carrier. With TLS > Required, it also checks the carrier's certificate on connections the carrier opens.

docs.title: Users of the UI and API
docs.text:
Everyone who uses the UI or the API is a user with a role. See Roles. Programs, such as a monitoring system, use an API token instead of a password.

Users can also log in through the organization's identity provider. See Single sign-on.

Until Ella IMS is initialized, anyone who reaches the UI can make themselves Admin, so initialize it right after installing.

docs.title: HTTPS
docs.text: Ella IMS serves the UI and the API over plain HTTP unless it is given a certificate in api.tls (see the configuration file). Use HTTPS whenever the UI or the API is reachable over a network you do not control.

docs.title: Single Sign-On
docs.text:
Users can log in to the UI through the organization's identity provider instead of, or as well as, a password. Ella IMS works with any OpenID Connect identity provider, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Ping Identity, Google or Keycloak. To set it up, see Configure single sign-on.

Login page with single sign-on

docs.title: Password and single sign-on
docs.text:
Password Single sign-on Credentials kept by Ella IMS The identity provider, with its own policies, such as multi-factor authentication Role set by An Admin An Admin, or the user's groups at the identity provider Session 30 days The session lifetime, 24 hours by default Access removed by Deleting the user in Ella IMS, at once Removing the user at the identity provider, at the end of their session

Password login stays when single sign-on is on, and at least one Admin always keeps a password. An identity provider that is down or misconfigured cannot lock everyone out.

docs.title: Matching users
docs.text: A user is matched to their account at the identity provider, not to their email address, so a changed or reused email address does not give access to another user. The email address is used once, to link the account at its first login, and only if the identity provider has verified it. A provider that does not say whether email addresses are verified, such as Microsoft Entra ID, must be trusted explicitly: anyone who can set their email address there could take over the matching user. An account with no user in Ella IMS gets one only from a group mapping.

docs.title: Offboarding
docs.text: Ella IMS does not learn when someone is removed at the identity provider. Their session lasts until its lifetime ends, and their API tokens until deleted. A shorter session lifetime narrows that window, at the cost of logging in more often. To end access at once, offboard the user in Ella IMS.

docs.title: Client secret
docs.text: The identity provider's client secret is stored in the database, db.path in the configuration file, and so in any copy of it.

docs.title: SIP Trunks
docs.text:
A SIP trunk connects Ella IMS to a carrier, for calls to and from numbers outside the HSS.

SIP trunks

docs.title: The border
docs.text:
• BGCF: picks the trunk for a call out.
  • IBCF: the border with carriers. It hides the IMS from them.
  • TrGW: relays the voice.

docs.title: Calls out
docs.text:
1. A phone calls a number that the HSS doesn't know.
  2. Ella IMS takes the route with the longest matching prefix, else the default route.
  3. It tries the route's trunks in order, skipping those that are down or disabled.

Short codes never go to a trunk.

docs.title: Calls in
docs.text: Ella IMS finds the trunk by the call's source address, and routes the call to the subscriber with the called number.

docs.title: Trust
docs.text: Ella IMS accepts the caller's number only from a trusted trunk. Mark a trunk trusted only if you have an interconnect agreement with the carrier.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text: Ella IMS relays the voice without transcoding, so phones and the carrier must share a codec, such as AMR-WB. A carrier that accepts only G.711 needs a transcoding SBC.

docs.title: Keepalives
docs.text: Ella IMS sends OPTIONS requests to each trunk. A trunk that stops answering is down until it answers again.

docs.title: Not supported
docs.text:
• Emergency calls
  • Video, fax and messages
  • Registration with the carrier
  • SRTP

docs.title: SMS over IP
docs.text:
Ella IMS includes an IP Short Message Gateway (IP-SM-GW), which lets phones send and receive SMS over IMS.

SMS over IP

docs.title: Sending
docs.text:
1. The phone sends the SMS as a SIP MESSAGE, which reaches the IP-SM-GW through the P-CSCF and the S-CSCF.
  2. The IP-SM-GW forwards it to the SMSC of the phone's service centre address.

docs.title: Receiving
docs.text:
1. While the phone registers with SMS over IP, the IP-SM-GW registers at the HSS for the subscriber.
  2. The HSS then sends the SMSC's routing requests for the subscriber to the IP-SM-GW.
  3. The IP-SM-GW delivers over IMS first, then over NAS through the MME or SMSF.

docs.title: Configure Single Sign-On
docs.text: This guide lets users sign in to the Ella IMS UI through an OpenID Connect identity provider. It gives the steps for Keycloak; other providers are set up the same way.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella IMS: served over HTTPS, at a URL with no path.
  • Identity provider: an OpenID Connect provider, reachable from Ella IMS over HTTPS.
  • Ella IMS account: an Admin that signs in with a password.

The examples use these values:

Value Role https://ims.example.com Ella IMS's external URL https://ims.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback Redirect URL: the external URL followed by /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback

docs.title: 1. Register Ella IMS at the identity provider
docs.text:
KeycloakOther providers

In the realm users sign in to:

  1. Go to Clients and click Create client.
  2. Set Client type to OpenID Connect and Client ID to ims. Click Next.
  3. Turn on Client authentication. Keep Standard flow checked. Click Next.
  4. Set Valid redirect URIs to the redirect URL. Click Save.
  5. In the client's Credentials tab, copy the Client Secret.

In Users, turn on Email verified for each user.

  1. Register a web application, or confidential client, with the redirect URL.
  2. Create a client secret for it.
  3. Allow the openid, email and profile scopes.

If the provider does not send email_verified, turn on Trust email addresses from this provider in step 2.

docs.title: 2. Configure Ella IMS
docs.text:
In the UI, go to Single Sign-On and, in Provider, click Edit. Set:

Field Value External URL https://ims.example.com Issuer URL Keycloak: https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm>. Otherwise, from the provider. CA certificate The PEM CA certificate of the identity provider, only if a private CA signs its certificate Client ID Keycloak: ims. Otherwise, from the provider. Client secret The secret from step 1 Display name The name on the login button, such as Keycloak Scopes openid email profile Session lifetime 24 hours, or less to end access sooner after offboarding Trust email addresses from this provider Off, unless the provider does not send email_verified

Check that the Redirect URL under the external URL is the one registered in step 1.

docs.title: 3. Test the identity provider
docs.text: In the dialog, click Test. Fix the issuer URL or the CA certificate until it shows Works. Click Update.

docs.title: 4. Enable single sign-on
docs.text:
On the Single Sign-On page, click Enable.

To turn it off, for example during an incident, click Disable. Everyone who logged in with single sign-on is signed out.

docs.title: 5. Sign in
docs.text:
1. Give a user access: create their user, or map their groups to a role.
  2. In a private browser window, open https://ims.example.com, and click Log in with your display name.
  3. Sign in at the identity provider. Ella IMS opens.

If the login page shows an error, the auth_oidc_login audit event in the logs gives the reason.

docs.title: Connect to a SIP Trunk
docs.text:
This guide connects Ella IMS to a carrier's SIP trunk, for calls to and from numbers outside the HSS. The example carrier is Telnyx, any other carrier should work similarly.

The examples use these addresses:

Address Role 203.0.113.5 Ella IMS's address towards the carrier sip.telnyx.com Telnyx's SIP domain 192.76.120.10, 64.16.250.10, 192.76.120.14 Addresses Telnyx sends calls from

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella IMS: connected to the core network, as in Integrate with Ella Core, with the numbering plan set.
  • SIP trunk: an IP-authenticated trunk.
  • Numbers: the carrier's numbers, set as the subscribers' MSISDNs in the HSS.

docs.title: 1. Enable the IBCF
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, set the address carriers reach Ella IMS on, and restart Ella IMS:

ibcf:
  external:
    addresses:
      - address: 203.0.113.5

docs.title: 2. Open the firewall
docs.text: Allow SIP (TCP 5060) from Telnyx's addresses, and voice (UDP 10000–19999) from Telnyx's media networks, to 203.0.113.5.

docs.title: 3. Configure the carrier
docs.text:
In the carrier portal, create an IP connection:

  • Send calls to 203.0.113.5, port 5060, over TCP.
  • Enable AMR-WB.
  • Send called numbers in E.164 format, with +.
  • Attach an outbound voice profile.
  • Assign your numbers to the connection.

docs.title: 4. Add the trunk
docs.text:
In the Ella IMS UI, go to the SIP Trunks page and click Create Trunk:

  • Name: Telnyx.
  • Host: sip.telnyx.com.
  • Inbound CIDRs: 192.76.120.10/32, 64.16.250.10/32 and 192.76.120.14/32, one per line.
  • Check Trusted.

Click Create.

docs.title: 5. Add a route
docs.text: On the SIP Trunks page, click Create Route. Leave Prefix empty, select Telnyx under Add Trunk, and click Create.

docs.title: 6. Check the trunk is up
docs.text: On the SIP Trunks page, the trunk's State should be up within a minute.

docs.title: 7. Place a test call
docs.text:
From a registered phone, call an outside number in international format, e.g. +15555550100. Then call one of your numbers from an outside phone.

Both calls should have audio both ways.

docs.title: Enable Push-to-Talk
docs.text: This guide enables group calls with floor control with Ella IMS's built-in Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) server. The examples use 10.6.0.5 as Ella IMS's SIP address.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella Core: integrated with Ella IMS, as in Integrate with Ella Core, and serving as the HSS.
  • Phones: the Ella MCPTT app, installed as in Install the Android MCPTT App, and a native IMS client that registers with a reg-id.
  • SIMs: with an ISIM you can program.

docs.title: 1. Enable the MCPTT server
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, set the address phones reach the MCPTT media on, and restart Ella IMS:

mcptt:
  media:
    address: 10.6.0.5

docs.title: 2. Configure Ella Core
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI:

  • Networking → Data Networks → Create: mcx, with an IP pool and IMS on.
  • Profiles → Create: an MC profile, e.g. mcptt. On it, Add Policy: a name, data network mcx, 5QI/QCI 69, ARP 3, May pre-empt, Not pre-emptable.
  • On the MC profile, also add the policies the users had on their previous profile, e.g. internet and ims.
  • Operator → IMS → Add Application Server: click Fill for Ella IMS MCPTT, then Add.
  • Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile: name mcptt; under Add from preset, select the MCPTT preset and click Add Criteria, then click Add.
  • Profiles → the MC profile → edit IMS Service Profiles: set MCPTT to mcptt, and MMTel (voice, SMS) to the service profile of the users' previous profile, if any, then Save.
  • Subscribers: put each user on the MC profile, with an MSISDN.

docs.title: 3. Route the MC traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS host, route the mcx IP pool through Ella Core's N6 address, e.g.:

sudo ip route add 10.47.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 4. Add the users
docs.text:
In the Ella IMS UI, go to Push-to-Talk → Users. For each person, click Add User and enter:

  • MCPTT ID: e.g. alice.
  • IMS Identities: the subscriber's MSISDN, e.g. 15550000001.

docs.title: 5. Add a group
docs.text: Go to Push-to-Talk → Groups, click Add Group, and enter a group ID, e.g. fire, and its members.

docs.title: 6. Set up the phones
docs.text:
On each phone:

  • Program the SIM's ISIM with sip:mcptt-<MSISDN>@<home domain> in a record of EF.IMPU after the first.
  • Set the APN to mcx.
  • In the app's settings, set the user's MCPTT ID as Ella IMS shows it, e.g. alice@ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and groups.

docs.title: 7. Make a group call
docs.text:
Start a group call from one phone. The other members' phones should ring, and Push-to-Talk → Calls should show the call.

A group call in the Ella MCPTT app

docs.title: Enable SMS over IP
docs.text: This guide lets phones send and receive SMS over IMS with Ella IMS's built-in IP-SM-GW. The examples use 10.3.0.7 as the SMSC's Diameter address and 15550000000 as its service centre address.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• HSS: an HSS connected to Ella IMS that supports the Sh-Update of SMSRegistrationInfo and forwards routing requests to the IP-SM-GW over S6c.
  • SMSC: an SMSC with an SGd interface, such as Ella SMSC.
  • MME or SMSF, for delivery over NAS when IMS fails: reachable over SGd.

docs.title: 1. Set the IP-SM-GW number
docs.text: In the Ella IMS UI, go to the Cores page. Under SMS over IP, click the edit icon next to IP-SM-GW Number, enter an E.164 number without +, e.g. 15550000100, and click Update.

docs.title: 2. Add the SMSC
docs.text:
Under Peers, click Add Peer, and enter:

  • Address: 10.3.0.7.
  • Roles: SGd only.
  • Service Centres: 15550000000.
  • Transport: SCTP, for Ella SMSC.
  • Host: the SMSC's Diameter identity, e.g. smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org for Ella SMSC.

Click Add.

docs.title: 3. Let the HSS reach the IP-SM-GW
docs.text: Edit the HSS peer, check Sh and S6c, and click Update. If the HSS's core also serves the MME or SMSF, check SGd too, for fallback to SMS over NAS.

docs.title: 4. Add iFCs in the HSS
docs.text:
With Ella Core:

  • Operator → IMS → Add Application Server: name ip-sm-gw, the IP-SM-GW Name of the Cores page as the Server Name, then Add.
  • Operator → IMS → Add Service Profile: name sms-over-ip; under Add from preset, select the SMS over IP preset and the ip-sm-gw Application Server, click Add Criteria, then click Add.
  • Profiles → the subscribers' profile → edit IMS Service Profiles: set MMTel (voice, SMS) to sms-over-ip, then Save.

With another HSS, add two iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the IP-SM-GW Name of the Cores page as the server name, e.g. sip:ipsmgw.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and default handling SESSION_CONTINUED:

  • A trigger point on method REGISTER, with the subscriber's MSISDN as the service information, and Include Register Request and Include Register Response set.
  • A trigger point on method MESSAGE, session case ORIGINATING_REGISTERED, and header Content-Type matching application/vnd\.3gpp\.sms.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text: Register a phone with SMS over IP enabled, and send an SMS. ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total should count it, with direction mo and result success.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Choose one of the installation methods below.

Snap (Recommended)SourceDockerKubernetes

Install the Ella IMS snap:

sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control

Configure Ella IMS:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

Start Ella IMS:

sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd

Install the required dependencies:

sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc

Clone the Ella IMS repository:

git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git
cd ims

Build the frontend:

npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui

Build Ella IMS:

go build -o ims -ldflags "-s -w -X github.com/ellanetworks/ims/version.GitCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ./cmd/ims

Configure Ella IMS:

vim ims.yaml

Start Ella IMS:

sudo ./ims --config ims.yaml

Create a new directory:

mkdir ella-ims
cd ella-ims

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml
configs:
  ella_ims_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        level: info
      db:
        path: /data/ims.db
      api:
        address: 0.0.0.0
        port: 5020
      sip:
        addresses: [10.6.0.5]
      diameter:
        address: 10.3.0.5

services:
  ella-ims:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-ims:latest
    configs:
      - source: ella_ims_config
        target: /ims.yaml
    entrypoint: /bin/ims --config /ims.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    volumes:
      - ella-ims-data:/data

volumes:
  ella-ims-data:

Set sip.addresses and diameter.address to addresses of the host.

Start the Ella IMS container:

docker compose up -d

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the Multus CNI installed.

Download the Ella IMS manifests:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims.git

Edit ims/k8s/ims-sip-nad.yaml: set master, the SIP address, and the route to the phones' IP pool through the core's N6 (5G) or SGi (4G) address.

Edit ims/k8s/ims-diameter-nad.yaml: set master and the Diameter address.

Edit ims/k8s/ims-configmap.yaml: set sip.addresses and diameter.address to the same addresses.

Create the namespace:

kubectl create namespace ella
kubectl label namespace ella pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=privileged

Deploy Ella IMS:

kubectl apply -k ims/k8s

Ella IMS's UI and API are on the ella-ims NodePort Service.

Ella IMS's UI and API are at http://<host-ip>:5020. Open the UI and create the first user.

See the configuration reference for all options.

docs.title: Install the Android MCPTT App
docs.text: This guide installs Ella MCPTT, the push-to-talk app for Ella IMS, on Android phones.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Phones: Android 14 or later.
  • SIMs: access rules (ARA-M) that allow the app's signing certificate, SHA-1 692EDA27666062D3982DF420E1FEC26FE806335B.

docs.title: 1. Download the app
docs.text:
Download the app and its checksum, and check them:

curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk
curl -LO https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk.sha256
sha256sum -c ella-mcptt.apk.sha256

docs.title: 2. Install the app
docs.text:
MDMadbOn the phone

In your MDM, add ella-mcptt.apk as a private or in-house app, and assign it to the phones.

Connect the phone over USB, with USB debugging on, and run:

adb install -r ella-mcptt.apk

In the phone's browser, open https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims/releases/download/mcptt-edge/ella-mcptt.apk, allow the browser to install unknown apps, and install it.

docs.title: 3. Grant the permissions
docs.text:
Open Ella MCPTT and go to Settings → Diagnostics → Permissions. Tap Allow on each item, and allow it in the prompt. It should show The app has everything it needs.

To update the app, install a newer APK the same way. Its settings are kept.

docs.title: Integrate with an Application Server
docs.text: This guide connects an Application Server (AS), such as voicemail or conferencing, to Ella IMS. The examples use 10.80.0.30 as the AS's address and 10.6.0.5 as Ella IMS's SIP address.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • HSS: an HSS that provisions initial Filter Criteria (iFCs).

docs.title: 1. Trust the AS
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, add the AS's address to the trusted networks, optionally set how long the AS has to answer, and restart Ella IMS:

sip:
  trusted_networks: [10.80.0.30/32]
scscf:
  as_timeout: 4s

docs.title: 2. Add iFCs in the HSS
docs.text:
In the HSS, add iFCs to the subscribers' service profiles, with the AS's SIP URI as the server name, e.g. sip:10.80.0.30:5060:

  • For third-party registration, add a trigger point on method REGISTER. Set Include Register Request and Include Register Response if the AS needs them.
  • For originating or terminating services, add a trigger point on the session case, plus the method, header or Request-URI to match.
  • Set the default handling to SESSION_CONTINUED to go on without the AS, or to SESSION_TERMINATED to fail the call, or deregister the user on REGISTER.

docs.title: 3. Add the AS's PSIs
docs.text:
If the AS serves its own URIs, such as a conference factory:

  • Add its PSIs to the HSS, distinct or wildcarded, with their iFCs or the AS as their server name.
  • If the server name is a host name, make it resolve to the AS, with a DNS A or SRV record.

docs.title: 4. Configure the AS
docs.text:
On the AS:

  • Trust Ella IMS's SIP address, 10.6.0.5.
  • Send requests to a user to the I-CSCF, port 5070.
  • Send requests on behalf of a user or a PSI to the S-CSCF, port 5080, with orig in the Route header, Route: <sip:10.6.0.5:5080;lr;orig>, and the user in P-Served-User or P-Asserted-Identity.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text: Register a phone. The AS should receive a third-party REGISTER, or the first request that matches its iFCs.

docs.title: Integrate with Ella Core
docs.text: This guide connects Ella IMS to Ella Core, with Ella Core as the HSS and the PCRF.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Ella IMS: installed and started, as in Install.

The examples use these addresses:

Address Role 10.3.0.2 Ella Core's Diameter address 10.6.0.2 Ella Core's N6 address 10.3.0.5 Ella IMS's Diameter address 10.6.0.5 Ella IMS's SIP address 10.46.0.0/16 IP pool of Ella Core's ims data network

docs.title: 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core
docs.text:
In Ella Core's configuration file, set the Diameter address, and restart Ella Core:

interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"

docs.title: 2. Set the Ella IMS addresses
docs.text:
In ims.yaml, set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from, and restart Ella IMS:

sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.5

docs.title: 3. Set the operator
docs.text:
In the Ella IMS UI, go to the Operator page:

  • Click the edit icon next to Operator ID (MCC/MNC), enter Ella Core's MCC and MNC, e.g. 001 / 01, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to Numbering Plan, enter your country code and prefixes, and click Update.

docs.title: 4. Add Ella Core as the HSS and PCRF
docs.text:
Go to the Cores page:

  • Under Peers, click Add Peer, enter 10.3.0.2, check HSS and PCRF, and click Add.
  • Under HSS, click the edit icon next to HSS Realm, enter epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org, with the MNC padded to 3 digits, e.g. epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.
  • Under Voice QoS, click the edit icon next to Policy Function, select PCRF, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to PCRF Realm, enter the same realm, and click Update.

docs.title: 5. Route the phones' traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS host, route the ims data network through Ella Core's N6 address:

sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 6. Point Ella Core to Ella IMS
docs.text: In Ella Core, set Operator → IMS → P-CSCF Addresses to 10.6.0.5, then follow Ella Core's Enable Voice guide.

docs.title: Manage Single Sign-On Users
docs.text: These guides manage users who sign in through the identity provider. Configure single sign-on first.

docs.title: Give a user access
docs.text:
1. In the UI, go to Users and click Create. Set:
    • Email: the user's email address at the identity provider
    • Password: off
    • Role: the user's role
    • Pin role: checked to keep this role, if groups are mapped to roles
  2. Click Create.

The user signs in with Log in with the display name. Their first login links their user to their account at the identity provider.

docs.title: Map groups to roles
docs.text: Users in a mapped group get their role from it at each login, and get a user at their first login. Users in no mapped group cannot sign in through the identity provider, unless their role is pinned.

docs.title: 1. Send groups to Ella IMS
docs.text:
KeycloakOther providers
  1. Go to Clients, open the ims client, and open the Client scopes tab.
  2. Click ims-dedicated, then Configure a new mapper, or Add mapper > By configuration, then Group Membership.
  3. Set Name and Token Claim Name to groups. Turn off Full group path. Keep Add to ID token on.
  4. Click Save.

The groups are group names, such as ims-admins.

Configure the provider to send the user's groups in a claim, such as groups, as a list of group names or IDs.

docs.title: 2. Map the groups in Ella IMS
docs.text:
1. Go to Single Sign-On and, in Roles from groups, click Edit.
  2. Set Groups claim to groups.
  3. Click Add group for each group, and set the group and its role. Put the most privileged first: a user in several groups gets the role of the first.
  4. Click Update.

docs.title: Pin a user's role
docs.text:
A pinned role is kept whatever the user's groups.

  1. Go to Users and open the user.
  2. In Account, edit the role: choose the role, check Pin role, and click Update. Changing a role that comes from groups checks it for you.

To unpin, uncheck Pin role. The role then follows the user's groups from their next login.

docs.title: Unlink a user
docs.text:
Unlink a user whose account at the identity provider was replaced, so that their next login links the new account by email.

  1. Go to Users and open the user.
  2. In Account, click Unlink, then Unlink.

docs.title: Offboard a user
docs.text:
1. Remove or disable the user at the identity provider. They can no longer sign in, but their current session lasts until the Session lifetime ends.
  2. To end their access at once, go to Users in Ella IMS, open the user, and click Delete. This also deletes their API tokens.

To keep the user instead, open the user and:

  1. In Account, click Unlink, then Unlink. This ends their single sign-on sessions.
  2. Click Remove Password, then Remove, if they have one.
  3. In API Tokens, delete each token.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text: Ella IMS is configured using a YAML file. Start Ella IMS with the --config flag to specify its path. Unknown keys are rejected.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• logging (object, optional): The logging configuration.
    • level (string, optional): The log level: debug, info, warn, or error. Default info.
  • db (object): The database configuration.
    • path (string): The path to the SQLite database file.
  • api (object): The HTTP API and UI.
    • address (string): The IP address to listen on. 0.0.0.0 or :: for all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
    • port (int, optional): The TCP port to listen on. Default 5020.
    • tls (object, optional): Serve over HTTPS. Default: plain HTTP.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the server's certificate first.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
  • sip (object): SIP, for every CSCF.
    • addresses (list of strings): The IP addresses the CSCFs listen on and phones reach. At least one; specific addresses, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
    • trusted_networks (list of strings, optional): The networks, in CIDR notation, of the other nodes of the trust domain, such as Application Servers. The S-CSCF accepts requests only from them, the I-CSCF accepts their asserted identities, and Application Servers are sent requests only in them. Must not cover every address of a family. See Security.
  • pcscf (object, optional): The P-CSCF.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default 5060.
    • ipsec (object, optional): The IPsec ports.
      • server_port (int, optional): The protected server port. Default 5063.
      • client_ports (list of 2 ints, optional): The protected client ports. Default [5064, 5065].
  • icscf (object, optional): The I-CSCF.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default 5070.
  • scscf (object, optional): The S-CSCF.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port, UDP and TCP. Default 5080.
    • as_timeout (duration, optional): How long an Application Server has to respond before the default handling of its iFC applies, e.g. 4s. Under 32s. Default 4s.
  • diameter (object): Diameter, to the HSS and the PCRF.
    • address (string): The IP address of the Diameter connections, advertised to peers. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
    • port (int, optional): The port. Default 3868.
  • n5 (object, optional): N5, to a PCF. Required to select the PCF as the policy function.
    • notify (object): Where the P-CSCF receives the PCF's notifications.
      • address (string): The IP address. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::.
      • port (int, optional): The TCP port. 0, the default, lets the system choose one. Must differ from the other TCP ports on its address.
    • tls (object, optional): Mutual TLS on N5. Required for a PCF URI with the https scheme. The files are read when the PCF URI is set.
      • ca (string): The path to the PEM file of the CA certificates that the PCF's certificate must chain to.
      • cert (string): The path to the PEM file of Ella IMS's certificate, presented as both client and server. Must be valid for n5.notify.address.
      • key (string): The path to the PEM file of the certificate's private key.
  • mcptt (object, optional): The built-in MCPTT server. When absent, the MCPTT server doesn't run and opens no ports.
    • mode (string, optional): ims, the default, or direct: the MCPTT server is the registrar of its clients, without the IMS, for labs and tests.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port on each of sip.addresses. In direct mode, the UDP and TCP port clients send to. Default 5090.
    • media (object): The media relay.
      • address (string): The IP address of the media sockets.
      • advertise (string, optional): The IP address in the SDP, of the same family as address. Required if address is 0.0.0.0 or ::. Default address.
      • min_port (int, optional): The first port of the voice legs. Even. Default 20000.
      • max_port (int, optional): The last port of the voice legs. Default 20999.
      • control_port (int, optional): The port of the floor control channels, outside the voice legs' range. Default 21000.
  • ibcf (object, optional): The IBCF, the border towards SIP trunks. When absent, the IBCF doesn't run and opens no ports.
    • port (int, optional): The SIP port of the IBCF on each of sip.addresses, towards the I-CSCF and the S-CSCF. Default 5085.
    • external (object): Where carriers reach Ella IMS, on SIP port 5060, UDP and TCP, and TLS port 5061.
      • addresses (list of objects): One IPv4 address, one IPv6 address, or one of each.
        • address (string): The IP address. A specific address, not 0.0.0.0 or ::, neither in sip.addresses nor in sip.trusted_networks.
        • advertise (string, optional): The public address, of the same family, when Ella IMS is behind a 1:1 NAT that keeps ports. Default address.
      • tls (object, optional): Ella IMS's certificate, to accept TLS connections from carriers.
        • cert (string): The path to the PEM certificate chain, the leaf first.
        • key (string): The path to the PEM private key.
    • media (object, optional): The UDP ports of the voice of calls over SIP trunks, on sip.addresses and on ibcf.external.addresses. Two ports per call on each.
      • min_port (int, optional): The first port. Even, from 1024. Default 10000.
      • max_port (int, optional): The last port. Default 19999.
  • telemetry (object, optional): The traces.
    • enabled (boolean, optional): Export traces. Default false.
    • otlp_endpoint (string): The host:port of an OTLP/gRPC collector, over plain gRPC. Required when enabled is true.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Ella IMS supports four observability pillars: Metrics, Traces, Logs and Profiles.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Ella IMS exposes Prometheus metrics at GET /api/v1/metrics.

Metric Type Description ellaims_build_info Gauge Always 1. The version and revision of the running build are in its labels. ellaims_registered_subscribers Gauge Subscribers registered now. ellaims_registration_attempts_total Counter Registrations and re-registrations, by result: accept, auth_failure, reject. ellaims_active_calls Gauge Calls in progress. ellaims_calls_total Counter Calls that ended, by outcome: answered, cancelled, busy, rejected, no_answer, unavailable, failed. ellaims_sip_responses_total Counter Final responses the P-CSCF sent to phones, by method and status class. ellaims_sip_request_duration_seconds Histogram Time from a request of a phone to the final response the P-CSCF sent, by method and status class, the answer of the far end included when the request is forwarded. INVITE is left out: its final response waits for the callee. ellaims_diameter_peer_up Gauge 1 if the connection to a Diameter peer is open, by peer and application. ellaims_peer_requests_total Counter Requests to the HSS, the policy function, the SMSCs and the MMEs and SMSFs, by interface (cx, rx, n5, sh, s6c, sgd) and result (success, failure, error, timeout). ellaims_peer_request_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of requests to the HSS, the policy function, the SMSCs and the MMEs and SMSFs, by interface. ellaims_ipsmgw_short_messages_total Counter Short messages the IP-SM-GW carried, by direction (mo, mt), domain (smsc for mo; ims, mme, sgsn, smsf_3gpp, smsf_non_3gpp, none for mt, the last tried) and result (success, failure). ellaims_trunk_info Gauge 1 per SIP trunk, by trunk ID and name. ellaims_trunk_up Gauge 1 if a SIP trunk answers its OPTIONS keepalives, 0 if it is down, by trunk ID. A trunk without keepalives, disabled, or not probed yet, has no series. ellaims_trunk_calls_total Counter Calls over a SIP trunk that ended, by the ID of the trunk that gave the final answer, direction (inbound, outbound) and outcome, as ellaims_calls_total. ellaims_trunk_active_calls Gauge Calls over a SIP trunk in progress, by trunk ID and direction. ellaims_trunk_failovers_total Counter Calls to a SIP trunk retried on its next server or the next trunk of their route after a transport error, a timeout or a 503, by the ID of the trunk that failed. ellaims_trunk_media_relays Gauge Media streams that the media relay of SIP trunks relays now, by trunk ID. ellaims_trunk_media_packets_relayed_total Counter RTP and RTCP packets that the media relay of SIP trunks relayed, by trunk ID, the leg they arrived on (phone, trunk) and protocol. ellaims_trunk_media_packets_dropped_total Counter RTP and RTCP packets that the media relay of SIP trunks dropped, by trunk ID, leg and reason: unexpected_source, no_remote, no_destination, direction, malformed, send_error, policed. ellaims_trunk_media_packets_lost_total Counter RTP packets lost before reaching the media relay of SIP trunks, from gaps in sequence numbers, by trunk ID and leg. ellaims_api_request_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of API requests, by method, route (/api/v1/users/{email}) and status code. Requests to /api/v1/pprof/ and to no route are left out. ellaims_oidc_logins_total Counter Logins through the identity provider, by outcome: success, or a login error. ellaims_database_query_duration_seconds Histogram Duration of database calls, by connection pool: write, read. ellaims_database_query_errors_total Counter Failed database calls, by connection pool. ellaims_database_storage_bytes Gauge Size of the database on disk, by file: main, wal. go_* Gauge, Counter, Summary Go runtime: goroutines, heap, garbage-collection pauses. process_* Gauge, Counter Process: memory, CPU, open file descriptors, start time.

docs.title: Traces
docs.text:
Ella IMS exports OpenTelemetry traces when telemetry.enabled is set in the configuration file.

Property Value Export OTLP over gRPC, without TLS Service ella-ims Sampling Parent-based, always on for a trace the IMS starts Propagation W3C Trace Context Error status HTTP and SIP: a server span from a 5xx response, a client span from a 4xx, except a SIP 401 or 407 challenge. Diameter: a client span from a Result-Code from 3000. SIP trust domain Trace context is read and sent on SIP only within the trust domain: the IMS's own addresses, and for the I-CSCF, the S-CSCF and the MCPTT AS, sip.trusted_networks. It never reaches a phone or a SIP trunk.

docs.title: Spans
docs.text: Span Kind Description {method} {route} Server A request to the API, except /api/v1/livez, /api/v1/readyz, /api/v1/metrics and /api/v1/pprof/. Links to the caller's traceparent. {method} {url.template} Client A request to the PCF on N5. POST /n5/v1/sessions/{id}/{notify,terminate} Server A notification from the PCF on N5. Cx/{command}, Sh/{command}, Rx/{command}, S6c/{command}, SGd/{command} Server, Client A Diameter request. {method}, such as INVITE Server, Client A SIP transaction, until its final response. A request from a phone or a SIP trunk starts a trace, linked to the INVITE of its call or the REGISTER it renews. Out-of-dialog OPTIONS to and from SIP trunks have no span. registration expiry, media loss, media timeout, … Internal Work that starts later than its cause, as on a timer or after a settings change: a new trace, linked to its cause. media timeout: the IBCF ends a call whose media stopped, linked to its INVITE.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Requests send a token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The token is either:

  • an access token, from log in or refresh the access token, valid for 15 minutes;
  • an API token, which starts with ellaims_.

These paths take no token: GET /api/v1/livez, GET /api/v1/readyz, GET /api/v1/status, GET /api/v1/metrics, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml, POST /api/v1/init, POST /api/v1/auth/login, /refresh and /logout, and GET /api/v1/auth/oidc, /oidc/login and /oidc/callback.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role role_id Allows Admin 1 Everything. Read Only 2 Reading the settings, the registrations, the call records and the MCPTT state. Network Manager 3 Read Only, plus changing the settings and re-authenticating registrations.

Only an Admin manages users. Every user reads its own user, changes its own password, and manages its own API tokens.

An API token has the role of its user, but cannot create API tokens, change a password, or manage users or single sign-on.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
Ella IMS's API responses are JSON objects. A successful response carries a result:

{
    "result": "Result content"
}

A failed response carries an error:

{
    "error": "Error message"
}

GET /api/v1/livez and GET /api/v1/readyz answer 204 with no body when they succeed. GET /api/v1/metrics returns text in the Prometheus exposition format, GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml returns YAML, and unknown paths and methods answer in plain text.

docs.title: OpenAPI Specification
docs.text:
The full API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 specification embedded in the binary. Fetch it from any running Ella IMS instance:

GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
• 200 - Success.
  • 201 - Created.
  • 202 - Accepted.
  • 204 - No content.
  • 400 - Bad request.
  • 401 - Missing, invalid or expired token.
  • 403 - Not allowed for the role or the token.
  • 404 - Not found.
  • 405 - Method not allowed.
  • 409 - Conflict.
  • 429 - Too many requests. Retry-After is the seconds to wait.
  • 500 - Internal server error.
  • 502 - The identity provider cannot be reached or used. See Test an identity provider.
  • 503 - Service unavailable, or not ready. See Check readiness.

docs.title: Log In
docs.text:
This path returns an access token, and sets the session cookie, ims_session, or __Host-ims_session over TLS. The session lasts 30 days, and a user has at most 10.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/login

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description email string Yes Email address, in any case. password string Yes Password.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Wrong email or password. 429 More than 20 attempts in a minute from the client address, or its IPv6 /64; or more than 100 wrong passwords in an hour for the account.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Login successful",
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Refresh the Access Token
docs.text:
This path returns a new access token for the session of the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/refresh

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 No session, or the session ended. The response clears the cookie.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
    }
}

docs.title: Log Out
docs.text:
This path ends the session of the cookie, and its access tokens, and clears the cookie.

Method Path POST /api/v1/auth/logout

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 204 Logged out, or no session.

docs.title: Get the Single Sign-On Option
docs.text:
This path tells the login page whether to show the button to sign in through the identity provider.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak"
    }
}

docs.title: Sign In Through the Identity Provider
docs.text:
The login page sends the browser to this path, which redirects it to the identity provider. It counts toward the login limit of 20 per minute per address.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/login

docs.title: Return From the Identity Provider
docs.text:
The identity provider sends the browser back to this path, the redirect URL. Each login completes once. On success, it sets the session cookie, for the session lifetime, and redirects to /. Otherwise, it redirects to /login?error=<error>, and the auth_oidc_login audit event gives the details.

Method Path GET /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Error Description rate_limited Too many logins from the address. unavailable Single sign-on is off, or the identity provider cannot be reached. failed The login expired, was already used or is invalid, the single sign-on settings changed during it, or the identity provider returned an error. denied The user or the identity provider refused access. not_set_up The identity provider gives no email, or no user has it and no group mapping is set. email_not_verified The identity provider marks the email as not verified, or does not say and trust_unverified_email is off. linked_elsewhere The user with the email is linked to another account at the identity provider. no_group None of the user's groups is mapped to a role. groups_overage The user is in too many groups for the identity provider to list them. too_many_users 50 users exist. error Internal error.

docs.text: A call record describes a call the IMS handled, after TS 32.298 §5.1.3.1.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description search query str Substring of the ICID or of an identity of the caller or the callee. start query str Inclusive lower bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. end query str Exclusive upper bound of the request time, RFC 3339. Unbounded when omitted. outcome query str answered, cancelled, busy, rejected, no_answer, unavailable, failed Outcome to include. Repeatable. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description id int Record identifier. icid string icid-value of the P-Charging-Vector (§5.1.3.1.19). session_id string Call-ID of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.59). calling_party array P-Asserted-Identity values (§5.1.3.1.24). caller_impi string Private user identity of the caller (§5.1.3.1.36). requested_party string Request-URI from the caller (§5.1.3.1.43). called_party string Request-URI after normalisation by the S-CSCF (§5.1.3.1.9). callee_impi string Private user identity of the answering registration (§5.1.3.1.36). requested_at string Reception time of the INVITE (§5.1.3.1.58). delivery_start_at string Time of the final response to the caller (§5.1.3.1.55). delivery_end_at string End time of an answered call (§5.1.3.1.54). sip_status int Final status of the INVITE sent to the caller (§5.1.3.1.57). outcome string answered (2xx), cancelled (487 to a caller CANCEL), busy (486, 600), rejected (603), no_answer (408 after a 180), unavailable (480), or failed (any other final status). ended_by string caller, callee or network. alerted boolean Whether a 180 reached the caller. media array Media types of the accepted m-lines. in_progress boolean Whether the call has not ended. incomplete boolean Whether the record was closed without the end of the call. duration_ms int Duration of an answered call that ended, in milliseconds. in_trunk_id string ID of the SIP trunk the call came from. Absent for a call from a phone. in_trunk_name string Name of that SIP trunk at the time of the call. out_trunk_id string ID of the SIP trunk that gave the final answer. Absent for a call to a phone. out_trunk_name string Name of that SIP trunk at the time of the call.

docs.text: Field Type Description id string Peer identifier, a UUIDv7. host string DiameterIdentity of the peer, which must match the Origin-Host of its capabilities exchange. Absent if none. status object Connection to the peer. status.state string down, connecting, open, suspect, reopen or closing. down until the IMS has tried the peer. status.since string Time of the last state change (RFC 3339). status.remote_address string Remote address of the connection. status.host string Origin-Host the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange, else the configured host. status.realm string Origin-Realm the peer gave in its last capabilities exchange. status.error string Why the last connection to the peer failed.

docs.title: Query Parameters

docs.title: Add or Replace a Member

docs.title: List Registrations

docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description mcptt_id query str Filter by MCPTT ID. group_id query str Filter by group ID. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcptt_id string MCPTT ID of the user. client_id string MCPTT client ID. group_id string Group ID. status string Affiliation status at the participating function (TS 24.379 §9.2.2.2.2): affiliating, affiliated or deaffiliating. {
    "result": {
        "message": "user deleted"

}

docs.title: Single Sign-On
docs.text: These paths configure sign-in to the UI through an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider. They require Admin, and an access token: an API token gets 403.

docs.title: Get the OIDC Settings
docs.text:
This path never returns the client secret.

Method Path GET /api/v1/oidc

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description enabled boolean Users can sign in through the identity provider. external_url string The URL users reach Ella IMS at. redirect_url string The redirect URL to register at the identity provider. Empty without an external URL. issuer string The identity provider's issuer URL. client_id string The client ID registered at the identity provider. client_secret_set boolean A client secret is stored. display_name string The name on the login button. scopes array The scopes requested. Initially openid, email and profile. session_lifetime_seconds int How long a session started through the identity provider lasts. Initially 86400. trust_unverified_email boolean Email addresses are accepted when the identity provider does not send email_verified. An email_verified of false is always refused. ca_certificate string PEM certificates the identity provider's TLS certificate must chain to. Empty: the system's. groups_claim string The claim, in the ID token or UserInfo, that holds the user's groups. group_roles array Group-to-role mappings, in order.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "enabled": true,
        "external_url": "https://ims.example.com",
        "redirect_url": "https://ims.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback",
        "issuer": "https://idp.example.com/realms/ims",
        "client_id": "ims",
        "client_secret_set": true,
        "display_name": "Keycloak",
        "scopes": ["openid", "email", "profile"],
        "session_lifetime_seconds": 86400,
        "trust_unverified_email": false,
        "ca_certificate": "",
        "groups_claim": "groups",
        "group_roles": [
            {"group": "ims-admins", "role_id": 1},
            {"group": "noc", "role_id": 3}
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: Update the OIDC Settings
docs.text:
This path replaces the settings, which take effect at once. Disabling OIDC or changing the issuer ends all sessions started through the identity provider.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/oidc

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description enabled boolean Yes external_url string When enabled An https URL with no path. Stored as https://host[:port]. issuer string When enabled An https URL with no query or fragment, as the identity provider gives it. client_id string When enabled At most 255 characters. client_secret string When enabled and none is stored, or when issuer or client_id changes At most 255 characters. Empty or absent: the stored secret is kept. display_name string When enabled At most 64 characters. scopes array Yes At most 20, including openid and email. session_lifetime_seconds int Yes 300 to 2592000 (30 days). trust_unverified_email boolean No Default false. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates. groups_claim string With group_roles The claim name, such as groups. group_roles array No At most 100 objects with a group, matched exactly, and a role_id, 1 to 3. Each group at most once.

docs.title: Group Roles
docs.text: group_roles At each login through the identity provider Empty An Admin sets the role. Someone with no user in Ella IMS is refused. Not empty The first mapping whose group the user is in sets the role. A user in none is refused. Someone with no user in Ella IMS gets one, with that role. A pinned role is kept, whatever the groups. The last Admin with a password stays Admin.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 Updated. The response holds the new settings. 400 Invalid field, or issuer or client_id changes without a client_secret.

docs.title: Test an Identity Provider
docs.text:
This path checks that Ella IMS can use an identity provider. It changes no setting.

Method Path POST /api/v1/oidc/discovery

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description issuer string Yes The issuer URL to test. ca_certificate string No PEM certificates to trust for the provider.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description issuer string The provider's issuer. authorization_endpoint string token_endpoint string token_endpoint_auth_method string client_secret_basic or client_secret_post: how Ella IMS sends the client secret. userinfo_endpoint string Empty if the provider has none. jwks_uri string signing_algorithms array The algorithms the provider signs ID tokens with. keys int The number of signing keys. pkce boolean The provider supports PKCE. issuer_parameter boolean The provider supports RFC 9207.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 200 The provider can be used. 400 Invalid issuer or CA certificate. 502 The provider cannot be reached or cannot be used, for example because its token endpoint supports neither client_secret_basic nor client_secret_post. The error says why.

docs.title: Operator
docs.text: The operator is the PLMN of the IMS, from which its home domain and Diameter identity derive, and the numbering plan that converts dial strings to E.164 numbers.

docs.title: Get the Operator
docs.text:
This path returns the operator settings.

Method Path GET /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description mcc string Mobile Country Code. mnc string Mobile Network Code. numbering object Conversion of dial strings to E.164 numbers. numbering.country_code string Country code. numbering.national_prefix string National prefix. numbering.international_prefix string International prefix. numbering.min_national_digits integer Fewest digits a number dialled without a prefix needs to be routed to a SIP trunk. 0: never.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011",
            "min_national_digits": 7
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Operator
docs.text:
This path replaces the operator settings. A change of MCC or MNC changes the home domain, and the IMS restarts Diameter and SIP under the new names.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/operator

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description mcc string Yes 3 digits. mnc string Yes 2 or 3 digits. numbering object Yes numbering.country_code string Yes 1 to 3 digits, not starting with 0. numbering.national_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. Differs from international_prefix unless empty. numbering.international_prefix string Yes Up to 4 digits. numbering.min_national_digits integer No 0 to 15. Default 7. Fewest digits a number dialled without a prefix needs to be routed to a SIP trunk. 0: never.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "numbering": {
        "country_code": "1",
        "national_prefix": "1",
        "international_prefix": "011",
        "min_national_digits": 7
    }
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "mcc": "001",
        "mnc": "01",
        "numbering": {
            "country_code": "1",
            "national_prefix": "1",
            "international_prefix": "011",
            "min_national_digits": 7
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: The policy function is the interface the P-CSCF uses for policy control: none, Rx to a PCRF, or N5 to a PCF.

docs.title: Get the Policy
docs.text:
This path returns the policy function settings and the policy function running.

Method Path GET /api/v1/policy

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description interface string none, rx or n5. n5 object Present for the n5 interface only. n5.pcf_uri string API root of the PCF, http[s]://host[:port][/prefix]. status object Policy function running. Differs from the settings while the IMS applies them. status.interface string none, rx or n5. status.endpoint string rx for Rx; the API root of the PCF for N5. status.notify string Address of the N5 notification listener. status.last object Outcome of the last request to the PCF. N5 only. status.last.at string Time of the request (RFC 3339). status.last.reachable boolean Whether the PCF answered. status.last.result string Result of the request.

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "interface": "rx",
        "status": {
            "interface": "rx",
            "endpoint": "rx"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Update the Policy
docs.text:
This path replaces the policy function settings. Calls and registrations after the change use the new policy function.

Method Path PUT /api/v1/policy

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description interface string Yes none, rx or n5. n5 requires n5 in the configuration file. n5 object No For the n5 interface only. n5.pcf_uri string Yes http[s]://host[:port][/prefix]. https requires n5.tls in the configuration file, http requires none.

docs.title: Sample Request
docs.text:
{
    "interface": "none"
}

docs.title: Sample Response
docs.text:
{
    "result": {
        "interface": "none",
        "status": {
            "interface": "rx",
            "endpoint": "rx"
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Pprof
docs.text: These paths serve the net/http/pprof API. They require Admin, and accept an API token.

docs.title: Profiling Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /api/v1/pprof/ An HTML page listing the available profiles. GET /api/v1/pprof/allocs A sampling of all past memory allocations. GET /api/v1/pprof/cmdline The command line invocation of the program. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutine Stack traces of all current goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/goroutineleak Stack traces of all leaked goroutines. GET /api/v1/pprof/heap A sampling of memory allocations of live objects. GET /api/v1/pprof/profile A CPU profile, of 30 seconds by default. GET /api/v1/pprof/threadcreate Stack traces that led to the creation of new OS threads. GET /api/v1/pprof/trace An execution trace, of 1 second by default. GET, POST /api/v1/pprof/symbol Function names of program counters.

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Paths Description seconds profile, trace Duration of the capture. seconds allocs, goroutine, heap Returns the difference of the profile over this duration. debug allocs, goroutine, heap, threadcreate 0: protobuf. 1: text. 2 (goroutine): stack traces in the format of a panic. gc heap 1: runs a garbage collection first.

docs.title: Registrations
docs.text: A registration is a private user identity registered with the S-CSCF, with its registered implicit registration sets.

docs.title: List Registrations
docs.text:
This path returns the list of registered private identities.

Method Path GET /api/v1/registrations

docs.title: Query Parameters
docs.text: Name In Type Default Allowed Description search query str Substring of a private or public identity. page query int 1 >= 1 1-based page index. per_page query int 25 1…100 Number of items per page.

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description impi string Private user identity. implicit_registration_sets array Registered implicit registration sets of the private identity. A set registers and deregisters as one (TS 23.228 §5.2.1a.0). implicit_registration_sets[].hss object Origin-Host (host) and Origin-Realm (realm) of the last Cx answer for the set. Absent while unknown. implicit_registration_sets[].identities array Public user identities of the set. identities[].uri string Public user identity. identities[].display_name string Display name. Absent if none. identities[].barred boolean Whether the identity is barred. identities[].registered_with array Other private identities a request to this public identity reaches (TS 24.229 §5.4.3.3 step 8). implicit_registration_sets[].contacts array Unexpired contacts bound to the set. A contact bound to several sets is listed in each. contacts[].contact string Contact URI. contacts[].instance string Instance ID, an IMEI URN when available (TS 23.003 §13.8). Absent if none. contacts[].reg_id int reg-id of the flow (RFC 5626). Absent if none. contacts[].q number q-value (RFC 3841 §7.2.3). contacts[].media array Media the device registered for: audio, video. contacts[].registered_at string Registration time (RFC 3339). contacts[].expires_at string Expiry time (RFC 3339). contacts[].address string Address and port of the device, as seen by the P-CSCF. Absent if unknown. contacts[].transport string udp or tcp. Absent if unknown. contacts[].protected boolean Whether IPsec protects the signalling of the device. contacts[].signalling_path string State of the IMS signalling path of the device: unmonitored, monitored or lost.

                                "barred": true,
                                "registered_with": []
                            },
                            {
                                "uri": "tel:+15550000001",
                                "barred": false,
                                "registered_with": []
                            }
                        ],
                        "contacts": [
                            {
                                "contact": "sip:001010000000001@10.45.0.2:5064",

docs.title: Re-authenticate a Registration

docs.title: SIP Trunks
docs.text: SIP trunks connect Ella IMS to carriers. SIP routes pick the trunks of a call by the prefix of the number. See SIP Trunks.

docs.title: List SIP Trunks
docs.text:
This path returns the list of SIP trunks, ordered by identifier.

Method Path GET /api/v1/sip-trunks

docs.title: Response Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Trunk identifier, a UUIDv7. name string Name of the trunk. addresses array Where requests to the carrier go, in order. addresses[].host string Domain name, or IPv4 or IPv6 address. addresses[].port int Port. Absent if not set. addresses[].transport string udp, tcp or tls. Absent if not set. inbound_cidrs array Networks that requests from the carrier come from. Empty if not set. domain string Host of the Request-URI of requests to the carrier. Empty if not set. trusted boolean Whether the carrier is in the trust domain. keepalive_interval int Seconds between keepalives to the carrier. 0: no OPTIONS requests. enabled boolean Whether the trunk carries calls, in both directions. tls object TLS with the carrier. See TLS. tls.required boolean Whether the carrier must use TLS, with a certificate. tls.ca_certificates string PEM-encoded CA certificates. Empty if none. tls.pins array SHA-256 fingerprints of pinned certificates, as upper-case hex bytes separated by colons. tls.identities array Domain names one of which the carrier's certificate must hold. Empty if not set. tls.ca_certificate_details array One entry per CA certificate, in order. See Certificate Details. effective.domain string domain in use, default included. effective.inbound_cidrs array inbound_cidrs in use, default included. effective.tls_identities array tls.identities in use, default included. status.state string up: the carrier answers OPTIONS requests. down: it does not; routes skip the trunk. unknown: not probed. unusable: conflicts with the configuration file or another trunk; carries no calls. status.since string Time of the last state change (RFC 3339). Absent while unknown.

docs.title: Certificate Details
docs.text: Field Type Description subject string Subject distinguished name. issuer string Issuer distinguished name. dns_names array DNS names of the subjectAltName. uris array URIs of the subjectAltName. ip_addresses array IP addresses of the subjectAltName. identities array Identities matched against tls.identities. ca boolean Whether the certificate is a CA certificate. not_before string Start of validity (RFC 3339). not_after string End of validity (RFC 3339). sha256_fingerprint string SHA-256 fingerprint, as upper-case hex bytes separated by colons.

docs.title: Request Body
docs.text: Field Type Required Description name string Yes 1 to 64 printable characters, without leading or trailing spaces. Unique among trunks, ignoring case. addresses array Yes At least one, each once, none reaching the same server as an address of another trunk: the same host, with a port and a transport that can match once their defaults apply. See Addresses and DNS. addresses[].host string Yes Domain name, or specific IPv4 or IPv6 address. addresses[].port int No 1–65535. addresses[].transport string No udp, tcp or tls. tls needs tls.ca_certificates or tls.pins. inbound_cidrs array No Networks, such as 198.51.100.0/24, or single addresses. No two may overlap, in this trunk or across trunks. None may overlap sip.addresses or sip.trusted_networks of the configuration file. Not 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. Default: the IP addresses among the hosts of addresses. domain string No Domain name, or specific IPv4 or IPv6 address, without brackets. Default: the first domain name among the hosts of addresses. Required if every host is an IP address. trusted boolean No Default false. A trusted trunk never uses UDP: no address may have udp as transport. keepalive_interval int No 5–3600 seconds, or 0 for no OPTIONS requests. Default 30. enabled boolean No Default true. tls object No Absent for a trunk without TLS. See TLS. tls.required boolean No Default false. Every address must have tls as transport. Requires ibcf.external.tls in the configuration file. tls.ca_certificates string No PEM-encoded CA certificates, at most 32. tls.pins array No At most 32, each a PEM-encoded certificate, or a SHA-256 fingerprint as 32 hex bytes, with or without colons. tls.identities array No Domain names, at most 16. Default: domain and the domain names among the hosts of addresses. Required with tls.ca_certificates if there are none.

docs.title: Addresses and DNS
docs.text:
host transport port Requests go to Domain name — — The NAPTR, then SRV, then A and AAAA records of the domain. Domain name Set — The SRV records for that transport, else the A and AAAA records at the default port. Domain name Set or — Set The A and AAAA records, at that port, over that transport, else UDP. IP address Set or — Set or — That address, at that port, else the default port, over that transport, else UDP.

The default port is 5060 for udp and tcp, and 5061 for tls. A trusted trunk skips UDP records, and uses TCP instead of UDP.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text:
Carrier authenticated by Field Carrier's certificate must hold A CA tls.ca_certificates One of tls.identities Its own certificate tls.pins One of tls.identities, unless the address is an IP address

An identity is the host of a sip URI or a DNS name in the certificate's subjectAltName, or its common name if it has none.

TLS connection opened by Extended key usage of each certificate of the carrier's chain, if present Ella IMS serverAuth, anyExtendedKeyUsage or id-kp-sipDomain The carrier clientAuth, anyExtendedKeyUsage or id-kp-sipDomain

With tls.required, the carrier must use TLS, and present a certificate on the TLS connections it opens.

CA certificates and PEM pins must not be expired when added. Ella IMS keeps the fingerprint of a PEM pin only.

Ella IMS's own certificate is ibcf.external.tls in the configuration file.

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text: Code Description 400 A field is invalid, an inbound network overlaps the networks of the configuration file, or tls.required is set without ibcf.external.tls. 409 Another trunk has the same name, an address that reaches the same server as one of this trunk's, or an inbound network that overlaps one of this trunk's.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add voice calls to a private 5G network with Ella IMS.

Tutorial Hardware Required Installation Method Duration Make Your First Voice Call An Ella Core 5G network, a second Linux host, two phones Snap ~30 min

docs.title: Make Your First Voice Call
docs.text:
In this tutorial, we will add Ella IMS to a private 5G network running Ella Core, and make a voice call (VoNR) between two phones.

You can expect to spend about 30 minutes completing this tutorial.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
To complete this tutorial, you will need the following:

Ella Core

  • A 5G network running Ella Core, as built in Ella Core's Getting Started (5G Network with Radio Hardware) tutorial. In this tutorial, Ella Core's N6 interface, ens3, has the address 10.6.0.2.

Ella IMS

  • A second Linux machine running Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, on Ella Core's N6 network. In this tutorial, it has the address 10.6.0.5.

Phones

  • Two 5G phones that support VoNR, each with a SIM provisioned as a subscriber in Ella Core.

docs.title: 1. Enable Diameter in Ella Core
docs.text:
On the Ella Core machine, edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml

Under interfaces, add the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.6.0.2"

Restart Ella Core:

sudo snap restart ella-core.cored

docs.title: 2. Install Ella IMS
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS machine, install the Ella IMS snap:

sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control

Edit the configuration file:

sudo vim /var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml

Set the address phones reach Ella IMS on, and the address it reaches Ella Core from:

/var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.6.0.5

Start Ella IMS:

sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd

docs.title: 3. Initialize Ella IMS
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to http://10.6.0.5:5020/. The Initialize Ella IMS page opens.

Enter an email and a password of at least 8 characters, and click Create. You should see Ella IMS's Cores page.

docs.title: 4. Connect Ella IMS to Ella Core
docs.text:
Go to the Cores page:

  • Under Peers, click Add Peer, enter 10.6.0.2, check HSS and PCRF, and click Add.
  • Under HSS, click the edit icon next to HSS Realm, enter epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.
  • Under Voice QoS, click the edit icon next to Policy Function, select PCRF, and click Update.
  • Click the edit icon next to PCRF Realm, enter epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org, and click Update.

Under Peers, Ella Core should show as open.

docs.title: 5. Route the phones' traffic
docs.text:
On the Ella IMS machine, route the phones' voice addresses, which we create in the next step, through Ella Core:

sudo ip route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400

docs.title: 6. Prepare Ella Core for voice
docs.text:
In the Ella Core UI, go to the Operator page and scroll to the IMS section. Click the edit icon next to P-CSCF Addresses, enter 10.6.0.5, and click Update.

Go to the Networking page and open the Data Networks tab. Click Create, enter ims as the Name, 10.46.0.0/16 as the IPv4 Pool, turn on IMS (voice and mission critical services), and click Create.

Go to the Profiles page and click on the default profile. Click Add Policy, enter voice as the Name, set the Data Network to ims, and click Create.

Go to the Subscribers page. For each of the two subscribers, click on it, click the edit icon next to MSISDN, enter a number, and click Update:

  • First subscriber: +15551230001
  • Second subscriber: +15551230002

docs.title: 7. Register the phones
docs.text:
On each phone, turn on VoNR, then turn airplane mode on and off.

In Ella IMS, go to the Registrations page. You should see both phones.

docs.title: 8. Make a call
docs.text:
From the first phone, call +15551230002. Answer on the second phone, talk, and hang up.

In Ella IMS, go to the Calls page. You should see the call, with the outcome answered.

Success

Congratulations! You have made a voice call over your private 5G network, through Ella Core and Ella IMS.
